clue.text: Constant problem at ticket machine if one's this

definitions.text: problem at ticket machine if one's this
definitions.meaning: read as '...', someone without coins cannot pay a ticket machine

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as CHANGE-LESS: lacking loose coins, which is a problem at a machine that takes only cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant stays the same, never undergoing any alteration or variation.

clue.text: Man left in class in India

indicators.note: the letter for left goes in the word for an Indian class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class in India

explanation.surface: A man who has departed and joined a social group in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, the rook.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the pieces are called men, and the rook is also known as this.

clue.text: Soldier collects second acceptable sum

indicators.note: the insect word gathers the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a soldier ant is a type of ant
a mo is a moment, a second
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A soldier gathers a second payment that is reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the soldier ant, giving ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A total or quantity of money is described as a sum.

clue.text: Ancient cheat following leader of Greek's mythical quest

indicators.note: the words for ancient and cheat come after the first letter
leader of means the first letter of the word Greek's

parts.note: olden means ancient, as in olden days
to fleece is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: An old swindle trailing behind a Greek leader on a legendary journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason and the Argonauts sailed to Colchis to seize this treasure in Greek legend.

clue.text: See exercise take great strides

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Watch exercise make huge progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To run with long, easy bounding steps.

clue.text: Refuse to be taken in by these papers' cash complex

definitions.text: Refuse to be taken in by these

indicators.note: complex means intricately mixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A refusal to be fooled by a newspapers' complicated money scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline, but it is rubbish, which dumps take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles of rubbish are where waste and refuse end up.

clue.text: Work in soapsuds evenly

indicators.note: take the even-numbered letters, the second, fourth, sixth and eighth, of the word soapsuds

explanation.surface: Some task performed while up to the elbows in soapy washing-up water.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, especially one of a numbered series.

clue.text: Vincent perhaps takes part of play in rehearsal

indicators.note: the actor's surname takes the word for part of play inside it

parts.note: Vincent Price was a horror-film actor
an act is a division of a play

explanation.surface: An actor learns a section of a play during a rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a session of repeated exercise to improve a performance.

clue.text: Drink with journalists to keep out of the news?

definitions.text: to keep out of the news?

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Plying reporters with drink to stop a story being published.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle or hide something, such as preventing a story being published.

clue.text: Plunder drink, being antisocial type

parts.note: spoils are goods taken as plunder
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A looter who drinks to excess is described as an unpleasant character.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who ruins others' fun is a fair example of an antisocial person.

clue.text: Air pressure produces sharp breath

parts.note: air is a gas
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A meteorological or medical note: a pressure change causing someone to inhale suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden convulsive intake of air, as in shock or surprise.

clue.text: While two lips entwined, its flame's short-lived

definitions.note: a description: a thing whose flame is short-lived

indicators.note: entwined means twisted together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A romantic moment: lips meeting, a brief burning passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A flickering marsh light, from burning gas, that soon vanishes.

clue.text: Bird allowed around hotel

indicators.note: the word for allowed sits around the word for hotel, enclosing it

parts.note: let means allowed or permitted
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A bird permitted to flutter about a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch, a songbird common in Europe.

clue.text: Second one making an impression — this person's fast

definitions.note: read as 'this person is fast', describing the noun

parts.note: a printer presses ink onto paper, making an impression

explanation.surface: Someone who wants to impress for a second time turns out to be quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner in short, fast races is described as a person who is quick.

clue.text: City men move around in fine cars

indicators.note: move around tells us to shift the letters of in fine cars about

explanation.surface: Wealthy businessmen driving around in luxury cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Men working in the City of London, the financial district, are bankers and investors.

clue.text: Workplaces of lots of people including top bishop

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for crowds includes, around its interior, the pieces for top and bishop

parts.note: flocks are crowds or congregations of people
to top is slang for to kill, as is to ice
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Office spaces holding many people, the senior cleric among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top bishop' looks like a senior cleric, but 'top' is slang for kill, giving ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Large buildings divided into offices are places where people go to work.

clue.text: Speaking proudly of snake bite

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a sting is a bite of an insect

explanation.surface: Someone bragging about being bitten by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragging means talking with excessive pride about oneself.

clue.text: Person walking slowly along street with posh car following

indicators.note: the posh car comes after the street

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A pedestrian ambling down the road with a Rolls-Royce trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambling or sauntering at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Not unusually, former prime minister detains pervert looking for trouble

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the word not are reordered
the surname of the former premier holds the word for pervert inside it

parts.note: Edward Heath was UK prime minister 1970-74
to warp is to pervert or distort

explanation.surface: A political scandal: an ex-premier holds a deviant, provocatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unusually' looks like 'as is usual', but it rearranges NOT to ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from Native American war customs meaning angry and spoiling for a fight.

clue.text: Band journey through Home Counties

indicators.note: the journey passes through the letters for Home Counties

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A group of musicians travelling through the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a pop group but is a strip of colour. The Home Counties are those surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of colour, a long narrow strip, as on a flag.

clue.text: Consider rising up to capture grand nobleman

indicators.note: the reversed word captures the letter inside it
in a down clue, rising up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to think is to consider
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A person considering an upward climb to seize a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising up' turns THINK into KNIHT, which takes in G.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight holds a title of honour, a lowly rank of the nobility.

clue.text: What can cut off supply of oxygen and copper in store

indicators.note: the pieces for oxygen and copper go in the word for store

parts.note: stock is a store or supply of goods
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a copper is a policeman, PC (police constable)

explanation.surface: Something in a warehouse that might stop deliveries of a gas and a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal, Cu, but here it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a valve that shuts off the flow of water or gas through a pipe.

clue.text: Church official comments about receiving kiss

indicators.note: the turned-around word takes the kiss into its middle
about signals turning the word for comments back to front

parts.note: notes are written comments
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A church officer makes remarks about being given a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NOTES into SETON, which takes X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church caretaker who looks after the building and graveyard.

clue.text: Plan to cut out middleman regularly

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of middleman, the even ones

explanation.surface: A scheme to eliminate the intermediary on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or notion, a thought about how to do something.

clue.text: Python at rest

definitions.meaning: Eric ... was a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' looks like the snake, but it is a member of Monty Python's Flying Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inactive and unoccupied, a machine or person not working is at rest.

clue.text: Potential murder weapon providing clue, very hot

parts.note: a lead is a clue in an investigation
piping hot means very hot

explanation.surface: A detective's hot tip about the weapon in a murder case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the board game Cluedo, where the lead piping is one of the weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game Cluedo, a length of metal tubing is one of the possible weapons.

clue.text: European country without any cause of disease

indicators.note: without means the letters of the word any are removed

parts.note: Germany is a European country

explanation.surface: A European nation free of any illness-causing agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe or bacterium that causes illness.

clue.text: Respect man exploding bluff

indicators.note: exploding blows the letters of respect and man apart to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Show some regard for a man who is losing his temper over a deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like a deception, but is a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or bank, as is a long steep slope.
